titulo: Git: the safety net for undoing any change
lead: For a task, an agent can change ten files at once. Without history, you don’t know what changed or how to go back. With Git, each good version is saved with a date and explanation, and you can undo a change you didn’t approve with one command.
objetivo: save versions with status, add, diff, and commit, and undo an agent’s change with git restore, without panicking.
hero_alt: Sheets of paper pinned in a row on a clothesline against a dark wall, beside a laptop.

aprende.t: Start the history only in the project folder
Read git status and git diff before saving
Save a version with a message that says what changed
Restore a file with git restore and undo a version with git revert

secoes.sub: The three stages of a file in Git. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: The agent created or changed files. git status shows each one: "Untracked files" are files Git isn’t tracking yet; "Changes not staged" are changes that haven’t been staged.
git add with the file name stages only that file for the next version (Git calls this staging). git diff --cached shows, line by line, what will go in.
The commit clips together what was staged. The message is the photo caption: a verb and an object, such as "Add contact section." "update" won’t tell you anything a month from now.

Change not saved yet: git restore returns the file to the last saved version (and discards your changes). Version already saved: git revert creates a new version that undoes the previous one without erasing the history.

secoes.volta: Golden rule: commit before asking for a big change
secoes.legenda: Git runs only on your computer, without internet. GitHub is another optional step (lesson 8).

rolagem_fim.texto: Commit before you ask. The agent makes changes. Check them with status and diff. Like them: add and commit. Don’t like them: restore. Each good version becomes a point you can return to.

secoes.titulo: From git init to the first undo

texto: Inside meu-primeiro-agente, git init creates the history. Never run it in your entire personal folder.
git config user.name and user.email, without --global, say who saves changes, only in this project. The email appears in each version and is visible if the folder is published.
git status tells you what stage each file is at. Always run it before staging anything.
This is where the .gitignore from lesson 5 proves itself: .env doesn’t appear in the list.
To learn, name the files in git add. The shortcut git add . stages everything that isn’t ignored, including a personal note you forgot in the folder.
git log --oneline shows a short list of versions, one per line.

exemplo.texto: Creates README, AGENTS.md, and a list of what not to save

texto: Only in the file, not saved: git restore arquivo. In a saved version: git revert with the version code, which appears in the log.
Check the open file, not just the terminal response.

exemplo.texto: Revert makes a correction and leaves all three versions in the history.

secoes.sub: In the meu-primeiro-agente folder. Replace anything inside < >.

blocos.rot: cmd · start and identify yourself (only in this folder)
blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente
git init
git config user.name "<Seu Nome>"
git config user.email "<seu@email.com>"
git status

blocos.rot: cmd · look, stage, and save the first version
blocos.conteudo:
git add README.md AGENTS.md .gitignore .env.example index.html
git diff --cached
git commit -m "primeira versão"
git log --oneline

blocos.rot: cmd · after the agent changes something
cmd · don’t like it: restore the file
cmd · like it: save the new version
blocos.conteudo:
git add index.html
git commit -m "<what changed, with a verb>"

git log --oneline
git revert <código da versão>

abas.html:
On branch master
No commits yet
Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
        .env.example
        .gitignore
        AGENTS.md
        README.md
        index.html

"Untracked files" = outside the history. .env is not on the list: .gitignore worked.

• Untracked files: files Git is not tracking yet.
  • Changes to be committed: staged; they’ll be included in the next version.
  • Changes not staged: changed, but not staged.
  • nothing to commit, working tree clean: nothing has changed since the last version.

• git init in your personal folder: Git starts looking at Documents, Downloads, everything. Run cd first and check the path.
  • Skipping Git: the agent’s first bad change becomes manual rework.
  • "Please tell me who you are": the name and email git config are missing.

secoes.titulo: Rehearse: save, break, and go back
secoes.sub: The agent will change index.html along the way.

missoes.pede: Start the history in this folder.
missoes.explica: The history lives in the hidden .git folder, just for this project.

missoes.pede: Check the status of the files.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
No commits yet
Untracked files:
        .env.example
        .gitignore
        AGENTS.md
        README.md
        index.html
missoes.explica: Five files outside the history, and no .env. That’s proof of lesson 5. (master or main is just the name of the main branch; in lesson 8 it becomes main.)
Now you can use the shortcut: you just checked the status and confirmed there’s nothing personal on the list.

missoes.pede: Save the first version with the message primeira versão.
missoes.explica: Version saved, with a short code (5f6c1eb). The numbers are examples.

missoes.pede: The agent rewrote the page, and you didn’t like it. Check the status.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
Changes not staged for commit:
        modified:   index.html
missoes.explica: "modified": index.html changed since the last version and hasn’t been saved yet.

missoes.pede: Restore index.html to the last saved version.
missoes.explica: No output means success. The agent’s change was discarded.

missoes.pede: Check that everything is back as it was.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
nothing to commit, working tree clean
missoes.explica: "working tree clean": the folder matches the saved version. Undone with one command, no panic.

secoes.fim: Full cycle: save, check the change, and go back. Do the same in your project.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: codes and counts in the responses are examples.

secoes.sub: In the meu-primeiro-agente folder, with the agent open in another cmd window.

exercicios.texto: git init, config, status, add, and commit. Ask the agent to make a big change to the page and, if you don’t like it, undo it with git restore.
exercicios.pronto: you undid an agent change with one command, and git status says "working tree clean".

exercicios.texto: Ask for two small changes and save each with a message that says what changed. Then undo the last one with git revert.
exercicios.pronto: git log --oneline shows the versions with clear messages, including the revert, and the page is back to how it was.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The agent made a big change you didn’t approve, and you haven’t saved anything since. What should you do?
opcoes: Delete the folder and start over.
Ask the agent to remember how it was.
git restore on the file, returning it to the last saved version.
perguntas.explica: With a commit from before the change, git restore restores the file in one command. That’s why you should commit before asking for a major change.

perguntas.p: Why name the files in git add instead of always using git add .?
opcoes: Because the dot doesn’t work on Windows.
So you don’t accidentally include a file you didn’t want in the history.
perguntas.explica: The dot includes everything that isn’t ignored, including a forgotten personal note. Use the shortcut only after checking the status.

perguntas.p: Which of these commit messages will help you a month from now?
perguntas.explica: Verb and object: the version list already tells you what changed, without opening a file.

perguntas.p: A saved version was wrong. Which command undoes it without erasing the history?
perguntas.explica: Revert is like a newspaper correction: it creates a new version that undoes the previous one. Restore is for changes that aren’t saved yet.
